title: Machine-learning analysis identifies an ANAPC-related prognostic signature in hepatocellular carcinoma
summary: An analysis of TCGA liver-cancer transcriptomic and clinical data used consensus clustering and LASSO-Cox modeling to derive an ANAPC-related three-gene survival-risk signature: SPP1, CDCA8 and CFHR4. The study initially clustered 371 cases and excluded six without survival information from survival analysis. Reported 1-, 3- and 5-year survival AUCs were 0.768, 0.683 and 0.668 within the source cohort. The signature was built and assessed only in TCGA-LIHC, without external validation. Drug-sensitivity and immunotherapy-response estimates were computational. Separate CDC27 cell experiments did not validate the signature. This is an exploratory retrospective association, without established clinical utility.
ai_technology: Machine learning (consensus clustering and LASSO-Cox prognostic modeling)
organization: The Second Affiliated Hospital, Guangzhou Medical University; Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center; Guangdong Medical University

evidence.tested: ANAPC clustering initially included 371 TCGA cases; six cases without survival information were excluded from survival analysis. A three-gene signature stratified survival within the source cohort, with no external validation. Separate Huh-7 CDC27 knockdown experiments did not validate the signature.
evidence.unknown: No independent external cohort or prospective clinical validation; no observed drug-treatment response data.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning analyses of TCGA expression and survival data (ANAPC consensus clustering and LASSO/multivariable Cox modeling) derived a three-gene risk signature for overall-survival stratification.

source_review.scope: Independently downloaded/read publisher 22-page Article in Press PDF: data-processing/model/validation Methods, signature Results and Discussion/limitations; primary publisher article abstract/date/affiliations. No supplement or independent validation.
